question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=0.65,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5}, & 0<x<1, \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{6}}, & 1\le x, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{4}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4{x}^{2}}{5}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{4{x}^{3}}{15}|}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =0.6\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =0.6-(0.65)^{2} \\  & ≈0.18\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.
